says: In next/, law Q9/Q12 (the assembled door refuses before an envelope, binding, reply or local step is saved) went red in about 0.4% of full runs when a refused send crossed an hour boundary, because the runtimes read the real wall clock; the crossing adds one write to the program's local quota account. Fixed the same day in this pull request: the law pins Date inside one hour per property run.
proof: With the real Date.now set 3 ms before an hour at refusal 0, the old law fails at refusal 1: 'expected { program: { writes: 16 } } to deeply equal { program: { writes: 15 } }'; the new law passes the same harness, and the whole file runs 13/13 green (nice -n 15 pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 next/apps/fabrika/src/runtime-recovery.laws.integration.test.ts). Both runs are in field/runs/2026-11-15-flaky-door-law-hour-tests1.json and -review1.json.
cost: A red full run about one time in 250, on a law that guards what a refused send may save.
